messages:
sam_support: FYI customer (acct: acme-inc) is hitting a sudden spike of 429s this morning when sending multi-part chats to rwd-3-16k. They also saw a short auth/billing failure ~08:12 UTC earlier. Attaching the log snippet they pasted and a repro they ran.

maria_re: thanks — can you paste the exact response headers and a minimal repro? need to know if this is per-key model limit or global quota.

sam_support: pasted below (redacted keys). note the X-RateLimit headers show low remaining for model variant. Customer says it was fine yesterday, burst started after a billing card bounce.

```
> HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
> Date: Mon, 10 Mar 2025 08:27:14 GMT
> Content-Type: application/json
> x-rate-limit-model-rpm: 60
> x-rate-limit-model-used-rpm: 60
> x-rate-limit-model-tpm: 360000
> x-rate-limit-model-used-tpm: 72000
> x-rate-limit-concurrency: 4
> x-rate-limit-concurrency-used: 4
> retry-after: 12
{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "message": "model rwd-3-16k per-key RPM exceeded"
}
```

sam_support: Their repro (they ran locally from their CI):
```
# simplified repro
for i in {1..8}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"
    -H "Content-Type: application/json"
    -d '{"model":"rwd-3-16k","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<14k tokens of history>"}],"max_tokens":1024}' &
done
wait
```

kevin_eng: quick summary from infra side: two things interacting here — (1) customer's key was temporarily flagged by billing; short auth failures can cause a flurry of retries from their client which burns RPM very quickly, and (2) rwd-3-16k on shared tier has relatively low per-key concurrency and RPM to protect noisy neighbors. We throttle at per-model-per-key RPM and global per-model concurrency. In this case headers show model RPM=60 and concurrency=4. Long contexts make each request more expensive (TPM usage higher) so the TPM budget gets eaten faster when they retry.

kevin_eng: repro I ran from my laptop (simulated their pattern) reproduced the 429s in ~18s. Reproduction script:
```
# spawn 8 parallel requests to simulate retry storm
seq 1 8 | xargs -n1 -P8 -I{} curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"rwd-3-16k","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"'$(head -c 14000 /dev/zero | tr '\0' 'A')'"}],"max_tokens":512}' -D - | sed -n '1,20p'
```

maria_re: ok — two-pronged mitigation to propose to customer: (A) short-term: reduce concurrency / add exponential backoff with jitter, truncate history (send only last N turns), or switch requests to smaller model variant (rwd-3) while we investigate; (B) medium-term: request a temporary per-key RPM bump or move them to Dedicated to reserve concurrency.

alex_g: also confirm: when billing bounces we return 401/402 on auth attempts; some clients interpret that as transient and start hammering retries. Suggest adding a client-side circuit breaker: if you see repeated 401/402, pause retries and alert ops.

sam_support: customer asked if context length itself can trigger throttling even without concurrency — they saw throttled responses while being the only active client.

kevin_eng: yes — because TPM counters are also enforced. If their requests contain very large context, TPM usage can exceed thresholds even at low QPS. Headers above show used-tpm 72k which is significant. We enforce both RPM/TPM and concurrency; TPM overage results in 429 as well.

infra-oncall: logging note for SRE: I've captured the customer's API key hash and trace ids: trace=tr-08a3e, span ids included in logs. Raising a short incident to quota team to check if we had a misconfiguration for rwd-3-16k shared tier at 08:10-08:30 UTC.

rate-limiter-bot: quota alert: model rwd-3-16k global concurrency at 92% between 08:15-08:28 UTC. per-key RPM spikes detected for key hash ending in ..9f.

maria_re: Proposed reply to customer (draft):
- Apologize and explain this is per-model per-key limits + TPM accounting; the 401 earlier may have triggered retries that burned RPM.
- Ask them to: (1) implement exponential backoff + jitter; (2) truncate or chunk long contexts (send last 3 turns or use summarization to compress history); (3) if they need sustained high throughput with long contexts, recommend Redwood Dedicated or a per-key RPM bump — we can route an expedited request to quota team if they share expected QPS and token profile.

maria_re: I will also attach our recommended client retry snippet and a saml of headers to watch for.

kevin_eng: share this quick retry snippet with them — ensures jitter and stops after a few attempts:
```
function api_call_with_backoff() {
  local attempt=0
  while [ $attempt -lt 5 ]; do
    resp=$(curl -s -w "\\n%{http_code}" -X POST ...)
    code=$(echo "\$resp" | tail -n1)
    if [ "\$code" = "200" ]; then echo "\$resp"; return 0; fi
    if [ "\$code" = "401" ] || [ "\$code" = "402" ]; then echo "billing/auth error -> stop retries"; return 2; fi
    # exponential backoff + jitter
    sleep $(( (1 << attempt) + (RANDOM % 3) )); attempt=$((attempt+1))
  done
  return 1
}
```

sam_support: Action items: (1) send draft reply to customer with short-term mitigations and request example QPS/token profile, (2) infra to verify if shared-tier concurrency/RPM config drifted, (3) quota team to evaluate temporary bump. tagging infra-oncall and kevin_eng.

infra-oncall: I checked — no global config drift. Looks like this is genuine per-key spike caused by retries + long contexts. I'll open a temporary quota eval for the account and mark as P2.

maria_re: sending the reply now and asking customer to try truncation and backoff; will update with their test results.

sam_support: thanks — keeping thread open for follow-ups.
